findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but that method is only defined as a protected one-arg method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) in UsernamePasswordForm, which is not a superclass of UsernameForm (UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator), so the source does not compile. The module fails to compile: javac emits 'cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()' in UsernameForm, breaking the entire build and CI for this PR; the intended conditional-passkeys skip logic in the username form never exists at runtime.

[BUG] The negative webauthn-form assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey are wrapped in try/catch(Exception) that treats any failure (including the assertion itself failing) as the expected outcome, so the assertions can never fail. MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()) throws NoSuchElementException when the form is absent (caught, 'expected'), but when the webauthn form IS wrongly present it throws AssertionError — which is also caught by catch (Exception nsee) and silently swallowed, so a regression that re-enables the passkey button for a user without passkeys during re-authentication passes CI. The only verification the test exists to provide is a no-op in both try blocks.

[BUG] The challenge(error, field) overload inverts the previous condition: the old code filled WebAuthn conditional-UI data when the user was NOT yet selected (context.getUser() == null), the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) gate requires user != null, dropping the fresh-login path for the single-execution UsernamePasswordForm flow. A fresh login through the browser flow whose single Username Password Form execution previously rendered the conditional-UI passkey autofill (form id 'webauth' with the user still unidentified) now gets no webauthn form, so passkey login on the username/password page is unavailable for first-time visitors in that flow — the exact scenario the removed comment 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected' guarded.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no such no-arg method is defined on UsernameForm or its visible parent AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator in this diff (the only definition added is the protected two-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) on UsernamePasswordForm, a sibling class). The class does not compile unless an unstated helper exists; if it resolves to some other overload, the skip-username-form decision for re-authenticating users is made without a UserModel, so the gating flag cannot be evaluated as intended and compilation/behavior depends on code outside this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new error-path behavior in createErrorResponse (calling AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError before fillContextForm when a conditional-UI passkey attempt fails during re-authentication) has no test coverage in this diff. The diff's re-authentication tests cover only a failed password followed by a successful passkey, and a failed passkey on a fresh login; the combination 'passkey fails while re-authenticating with USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH set' is untested, so a regression that clears the attempted username or shows a registration link on that error page (the exact bug being fixed) would not be caught. I searched the diff's three test files and none drives a failed conditional-UI passkey assertion during a prompt=login re-authentication.

[ADVISORY] The extracted setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in badPasswordHandler preserves the previous USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes, but no test in the diff asserts those attributes (or the hidden username field) on the error page during re-authentication. webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey checks only that the webauthn form survives a wrong password during re-auth; if setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError regressed (e.g., the auth note key renamed when the constant was made public), the re-auth error page would leak the username field and enable registration, and no assertion in this diff fails.

[ADVISORY] The new condition `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` gates the skip purely on the realm-level passkeys flag, not on whether the already-identified user actually has any passkey credential. A re-authenticating user with no passkey (and no linked brokers) is forced through the username form they previously skipped whenever the realm merely enables passkeys, and the form now accepts a different username during a re-authentication flow — the invariant that re-auth authenticates the already-set user is not enforced by this check; the diff adds no test for a re-authenticating user without passkey credentials hitting UsernameForm (the new reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest uses UsernamePasswordForm, not UsernameForm).

[ADVISORY] The auth-note constant USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is widened from protected to public solely so AuthenticatorUtils (a different package) can read it, expanding the public API surface beyond what the fix requires. Out-of-tree authenticator extensions gain a documented public hook into an internal re-authentication note with no compatibility contract, so a future refactor of this string key becomes a silent breaking change for external subclasses; the same reachability could be achieved with a package-private accessor or by moving the check next to where the note is written.

[BUG] Both call sites that set up conditional passkey UI in UsernamePasswordForm were inverted from `user == null` to `user != null`, so the initial-login page (user not yet identified) no longer calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm and the conditional-UI passkey prompt disappears from the combined username/password form on first login. Realms whose browser flow uses UsernamePasswordForm lose WebAuthn conditional-UI autofill on the ordinary first-login page: the login-then-passkey path that previously triggered `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() -> fillContextForm(context)` (which sets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI for the unidentified-user branch) now requires user != null, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is false exactly on the screen where the old code enabled it; users with discoverable passkeys get no passkey prompt until after they type a username/password.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate() now gates the skip-form fast path on `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (a no-arg method not shown in this diff) while UsernamePasswordForm uses a different, differently-shaped `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` helper, creating two parallel 'passkeys enabled' decision points that can drift. A future edit to one signature or condition (e.g. adding the user check only to UsernamePasswordForm's variant, or null-handling in UsernameForm's variant) changes whether the username form is skipped during re-authentication inconsistently between the split (UsernameForm+PasswordForm) and combined (UsernamePasswordForm) browser flows; the next maintainer must update two near-identical predicates with different shapes.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() is a new overridable hook whose only override (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator) returns an unconditional false, encoding the 'don't list authenticators during conditional-UI login' rule as a subclass override rather than a shared policy decision. Any third WebAuthnAuthenticator subclass (e.g. the 2FA non-conditional variant or future custom authenticators) inherits the default `user != null` behavior silently; a contributor adding a new authenticator that should suppress the authenticator list will not discover the hook, and the conditional-vs-listed decision now lives in class hierarchy shape rather than one inspectable policy — the next change to when authenticators are shown requires reasoning about virtual dispatch across three classes.

[BUG] When conditional passkeys are enabled at the realm level, UsernameForm no longer auto-succeeds for a re-authenticating user, even when that user has no passkey credential and no linked brokers, because the new guard `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` bypasses the skip unconditionally for passkey realms. A realm admin who enables passkeys changes the re-authentication (prompt=login) experience for every user in the realm, including password-only users with no WebAuthn credential: users who previously sailed through the username step during re-auth now get an extra interactive form step. The prior intent ('We can skip the form when user is re-authenticating') is silently dropped based on a realm policy flag rather than on whether the user can actually use a passkey; no test in the diff covers passkeysEnabled=true with a user holding no passkey credential, so this regression is unverified.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the diff only defines the one-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` in UsernamePasswordForm, and UsernameForm is not shown in the diff to extend UsernamePasswordForm or to declare any such member. If UsernameForm does not already have a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (or a webauthnAuth field, which the method needs), this diff does not compile; the visibility widening of USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH suggests refactoring pressure toward shared state that this half-refactor leaves inconsistent.

[ADVISORY] The fill of webauthn data was inverted from 'only when user is not already selected' to 'whenever user is set AND passkeys enabled', so during a first-login flow where the user was pre-selected (e.g., via kc_identity reset, IDP hint, or identity-first flows), passkey conditional-UI data is now injected where the previous intent explicitly excluded it. Admins of realms with passkeys enabled get passkey autofill on password challenge pages for pre-selected users in ordinary (non-reauth) flows where the original code deliberately suppressed it; the old comment 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected' documented an accepted constraint that this diff removes without any test asserting the new behavior for the pre-selected-user first-login path.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false unconditionally in the conditional-UI authenticator means fillContextForm now falls through to the 'user not identified' branch even when a user IS identified, changing which form attributes are set during 2-factor passkey scenarios using WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator directly. Any deployment using the conditional-UI passkey authenticator in a 2FA flow (user already identified, passkey required as second factor) loses the authenticator-picker listing that the base class previously rendered; the new test coverage only exercises conditional passkeys as first factor, so this second-factor regression would ship unnoticed until those users hit the fallback page.

[BUG] The 'WebAuthn elements not available' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is a try/catch that swallows its own AssertionError, so it passes regardless of whether the webauthn form is present. When driver.findElement succeeds and the element IS present, assertThat(element, nullValue()) throws AssertionError which is caught by catch(Exception), and the fail() call is never reached — the test never fails, so a regression that renders the webauthn button during password re-authentication for a user without passkeys goes undetected; the same broken pattern is repeated a second time later in the same test (~line 240) for the post-prompt=login page.

[ADVISORY] The reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test never asserts the username input is hidden (USERNAME_HIDDEN) or registration disabled after a failed password during re-authentication, which is the exact behavior the moved AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError logic in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler implements. A regression that re-shows the username field on the re-authentication error page (the original bug the refactor was extracted to fix) passes this test because it only checks that the webauthn form and 'Invalid password.' error remain present, not the form attributes this diff's production change sets.

[ADVISORY] Changing the fillContextForm gate from `user == null` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` (which requires user != null) removes conditional-UI/passkey setup from the first-login path of flows built on UsernamePasswordForm alone. Realms whose browser flow uses the combined UsernamePasswordForm execution (no preceding UsernameForm) no longer initialize WebAuthn conditional mediation on the initial username+password page, so users with discoverable passkeys lose the silent autofill/autologin on first visit and are forced to type username+password; only re-auth (user already set) gets the passkey UI. The diff's own tests only cover the re-auth path and the organization flow where the user is pre-set, so the regression on the unidentified-user path of UsernamePasswordForm is untested.

[ADVISORY] When the user is already set (re-auth) and conditional passkeys are enabled, UsernameForm no longer short-circuits with context.success() even when the user has linked brokers, and drops the hasLinkedBrokers() skip on the success path for passkey-enabled realms. A re-authenticating user whose realm has passkeys enabled but who authenticates via a linked IdP is now always shown the username form during re-auth instead of being routed through their broker, adding a confusing extra step for passkey-less broker users; the broker path is only preserved when passkeys are disabled realm-wide, which is the wrong dimension to gate on (per-user passkey availability is what matters).

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is called in createErrorResponse before the form's error attribute is fully assembled, and it reads the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note which is only written by the username/password flow, not by the conditional-UI passkey action path. When a passkey fails during re-authentication in a flow where the note was never set (e.g., the conditional-UI authenticator handles re-auth directly after the username/password execution was skipped), the form renders as a regular (non-hidden-username, registration-enabled) form, exposing the username field and registration link mid-re-auth — the exact visual-state bug this PR fixes resurfaces on that path; nothing logs or surfaces the divergence, so it is silently partial error handling.

Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

That means in realms where conditional passkeys are enabled, a re-authenticating user will no longer auto-succeed past the username step even if they have no linked brokers (previous behavior). The guard is realm/feature-driven (via `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`), not based on whether the specific user has any WebAuthn/passkey credential, so it plausibly adds an extra interactive step for password-only users. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable this is an actual defect vs an intentional product change to enable passkeys during re-auth; it is a concrete behavioral change/edge case that is not covered by tests in this diff (there is a test for re-auth without passkeys, but it sets passkeysEnabled=false, not true).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the diff only defines the one-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` in UsernamePasswordForm, and UsernameForm is not shown in the diff to extend UsernamePasswordForm or to declare any such member. If UsernameForm does not already have a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (or a webauthnAuth field, which the method needs), this diff does not compile; the visibility widening of USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH suggests refactoring pressure toward shared state that this half-refactor leaves inconsistent.
matched_golden_ids: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments while only a one-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) exists, implying the required UserModel parameter is missing. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fill of webauthn data was inverted from 'only when user is not already selected' to 'whenever user is set AND passkeys enabled', so during a first-login flow where the user was pre-selected (e.g., via kc_identity reset, IDP hint, or identity-first flows), passkey conditional-UI data is now injected where the previous intent explicitly excluded it. Admins of realms with passkeys enabled get passkey autofill on password challenge pages for pre-selected users in ordinary (non-reauth) flows where the original code deliberately suppressed it; the old comment 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected' documented an accepted constraint that this diff removes without any test asserting the new behavior for the pre-selected-user first-login path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change when WebAuthn conditional-UI data is filled for the username/password form: in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(...)` it flips from `if (context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled())` to `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null` (so now only identified/pre-selected users get `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`, including on error challenges). That is a real behavioral change that could affect flows where `context.getUser()` is pre-set before reaching this authenticator. However, the PR appears to be intentionally enabling this (tests were updated to expect the WebAuthn form still present after username selection, and new re-authentication tests were added), so it is not verifiably a defect from the diff alone; the actionable review point is the potential untested/undocumented impact on pre-selected-user non-reauth login paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false unconditionally in the conditional-UI authenticator means fillContextForm now falls through to the 'user not identified' branch even when a user IS identified, changing which form attributes are set during 2-factor passkey scenarios using WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator directly. Any deployment using the conditional-UI passkey authenticator in a 2FA flow (user already identified, passkey required as second factor) loses the authenticator-picker listing that the base class previously rendered; the new test coverage only exercises conditional passkeys as first factor, so this second-factor regression would ship unnoticed until those users hit the fallback page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` depend on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` instead of `context.getUser() != null`. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that method to return `false` unconditionally, so even when `context.getUser()` is set it will always take the “user not identified” path in `fillContextForm()`, changing which form attributes/beans get set compared to before. Whether this is a bug depends on intended/real deployments (e.g., using the conditional-UI authenticator as a 2nd factor), which the diff does not prove, but it is a concrete behavioral/compatibility concern introduced by this change and is not covered by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'WebAuthn elements not available' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is a try/catch that swallows its own AssertionError, so it passes regardless of whether the webauthn form is present. When driver.findElement succeeds and the element IS present, assertThat(element, nullValue()) throws AssertionError which is caught by catch(Exception), and the fail() call is never reached — the test never fails, so a regression that renders the webauthn button during password re-authentication for a user without passkeys goes undetected; the same broken pattern is repeated a second time later in the same test (~line 240) for the post-prompt=login page.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()`, the try/catch does *not* swallow the failing assertion when the element exists. `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)` fails by throwing an `AssertionError` (an `Error`, not an `Exception`), and the code only catches `Exception`, so the test would fail if `driver.findElement(...)` succeeds and the webauthn form is present. The catch is only reached when `findElement` throws (e.g., `NoSuchElementException`), which is the intended “element absent” case. The finding’s claim that the test “passes regardless” because the assertion is caught is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test never asserts the username input is hidden (USERNAME_HIDDEN) or registration disabled after a failed password during re-authentication, which is the exact behavior the moved AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError logic in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler implements. A regression that re-shows the username field on the re-authentication error page (the original bug the refactor was extracted to fix) passes this test because it only checks that the webauthn form and 'Invalid password.' error remain present, not the form attributes this diff's production change sets.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves the re-authentication error-page setup (setting LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED based on the auth note USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH) into AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(), and calls it from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler() and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(). The added test `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` exercises a failed password during re-authentication and only asserts the error text ("Invalid password.") and that the WebAuthn form remains present; it does not assert the username field is hidden or registration disabled, so it would not catch a regression where the username field becomes visible again on that error page—the exact behavior this extracted helper is meant to enforce.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Changing the fillContextForm gate from `user == null` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` (which requires user != null) removes conditional-UI/passkey setup from the first-login path of flows built on UsernamePasswordForm alone. Realms whose browser flow uses the combined UsernamePasswordForm execution (no preceding UsernameForm) no longer initialize WebAuthn conditional mediation on the initial username+password page, so users with discoverable passkeys lose the silent autofill/autologin on first visit and are forced to type username+password; only re-auth (user already set) gets the passkey UI. The diff's own tests only cover the re-auth path and the organization flow where the user is pre-set, so the regression on the unidentified-user path of UsernamePasswordForm is untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, both places that previously called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` for the unidentified-user case were changed to `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. Concretely: (1) `authenticate()` now only fills WebAuthn/passkeys context when a user is already set, and (2) `challenge(context, error, field)` likewise no longer fills when `context.getUser()` is null. For flows where the browser flow uses only the combined `UsernamePasswordForm` (no preceding `UsernameForm` to identify/set the user), the initial username+password page will have `context.getUser() == null` and will no longer get conditional-passkeys setup via `fillContextForm`, which is a behavior change/regression directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When the user is already set (re-auth) and conditional passkeys are enabled, UsernameForm no longer short-circuits with context.success() even when the user has linked brokers, and drops the hasLinkedBrokers() skip on the success path for passkey-enabled realms. A re-authenticating user whose realm has passkeys enabled but who authenticates via a linked IdP is now always shown the username form during re-auth instead of being routed through their broker, adding a confusing extra step for passkey-less broker users; the broker path is only preserved when passkeys are disabled realm-wide, which is the wrong dimension to gate on (per-user passkey availability is what matters).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavior change in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it used to short-circuit when `context.getUser() != null` and `!hasLinkedBrokers(context)` by calling `context.success()`. Now that entire re-auth short-circuit is additionally gated by `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }`). Therefore, when conditional passkeys are enabled, the authenticator will not short-circuit even for already-identified users with *no* linked brokers, and the `hasLinkedBrokers` check is skipped entirely in that case—potentially adding an extra username step during re-auth flows. However, the finding’s emphasis on “even when the user has linked brokers” is not accurate (linked brokers already prevented the success path before), and claims about broker routing/per-user passkey availability aren’t directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is called in createErrorResponse before the form's error attribute is fully assembled, and it reads the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note which is only written by the username/password flow, not by the conditional-UI passkey action path. When a passkey fails during re-authentication in a flow where the note was never set (e.g., the conditional-UI authenticator handles re-auth directly after the username/password execution was skipped), the form renders as a regular (non-hidden-username, registration-enabled) form, exposing the username field and registration link mid-re-auth — the exact visual-state bug this PR fixes resurfaces on that path; nothing logs or surfaces the divergence, so it is silently partial error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError()` only applies the re-auth UI tweaks (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED) when the auth-note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` parses to true; if the note is absent it silently does nothing (`Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` => false). The diff also shows `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` now calls this helper, but the diff does not show where/if that auth-note is set for the conditional-UI/passkey path. So there is a concrete, diff-grounded risk of incomplete UI-state handling on some paths, but the claim that the note is “only written by the username/password flow” (and thus the bug “resurfaces”) is not verifiable from this diff alone.
